title: The old Photon stack (NetworkManager, RoomManager, SceneLoadManager, PlayerDataManager, GameManager, NetworkTypes, NetworkTestUI) is dead: about 2,900 lines
evidence: The only YAML holders are in TESTPHOTN.unity (NetworkManager, RoomManager, SceneLoadManager, PlayerDataManager, NetworkTestUI). TESTPHOTN is disabled in Build Settings and is already Block 2. GameManager has no YAML holder at all, and the comments at CardView.cs:512 and CardViewManager.cs:1183 say it was removed from GameScene. Every type in NetworkTypes.cs (PlayerType, NetworkPlayerInfo, GameMode, GameConfiguration, NetworkConstants, NetworkState) is referenced only by these same files. The live online code (MatchmakingManager, NetworkGameController, HomeConnectionWatcher) uses none of them. Outside the stack there are two kinds of references. AccountDeletionService.cs:173-174 calls FindObjectOfType<PlayerDataManager>(), which is always null in MainMenu/GameScene. PhotonAuthConnector.cs:50, GameModeService.cs:27 and TurnController.cs:526 mention them only in comments. Line counts: 529+504+740+233+371+318+183.
proposed_action: Delete the 7 runtime files together with TESTPHOTN (Block 2). Remove the 2 dead lines in AccountDeletionService.SignOutAndClearLocalData. Delete the Editor tools CreateCirullaScene.cs and Tools/FixGameManagerScenes.cs, which are already in Block 9. Fix the stale comments.
dependencies: Block 2 (TESTPHOTN + Build Settings row) and Block 9 (the 2 editor tools). Block 10: the 6 'reference' docs in Assets/Networking (ARCHITECTURE, EVENTS_REFERENCE, READY_SYSTEM_GUIDE, CODE_EXAMPLES, MULTIPLAYER_README, SETUP_PHOTON_PUN2) describe this dead stack, so keeping them would document code that no longer exists. Do not refresh the PUN RPC list in the same build without bumping the version; AppVersion = Application.version already isolates builds.
verdict_reason: I re-checked the GUIDs of all 7 .cs.meta files against every .unity/.prefab/.asset under Assets. NetworkManager (35837f2f), NetworkTestUI (c5df1099), RoomManager (1adb7474), SceneLoadManager (8822d927) and PlayerDataManager (b29c8b14) appear only in Assets/Scenes/TESTPHOTN.unity. GameManager (0a450284) and NetworkTypes (63f75546) appear in no YAML. A word-boundary grep of every .cs in Assets (Photon/PlayFab excluded) for NetworkManager|RoomManager|SceneLoadManager|PlayerDataManager|NetworkTestUI|GameManager finds only the stack itself, the two editor tools, AccountDeletionService.cs:173-174 (FindObjectOfType<Project51.Networking.PlayerDataManager>, whose Instance getter never creates an object) and comments at PhotonAuthConnector.cs:50, GameModeService.cs:27, CardView.cs:512, CardViewManager.cs:1183 and TurnController.cs:526. The NetworkTypes types (PlayerType, NetworkPlayerInfo, GameConfiguration, NetworkConstants, NetworkState) have no users outside the stack. The bare 'GameMode' hits are HomePanelUI's own enum, not Project51.Networking.GameMode. PlayerDataManager.PlayerStats does not collide; the GooglePlayGames PlayerStats is in another namespace. MatchmakingManager, NetworkGameController and HomeConnectionWatcher use none of these types. TurnController reflects only on 'Project51.Networking.NetworkGameController, Assembly-CSharp', which is live. Server/ has no string refs. The only TESTPHOTN reference is ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset:9. The only [PunRPC] methods in the stack are RoomManager 680/689/698, and the finding already covers the RPC-list caveat. Corrections: there is no Networking asmdef (Assets/Scripts/Networking compiles into Assembly-CSharp), so the 'Project51.Networking' assembly strings in CreateCirullaScene/FixGameManagerScenes never resolved anyway. NetworkTestUI is already in Block 2 and the two editor tools are in Block 9, so this item partly overlaps the prior list. Of the 6 'reference' docs Block 10 keeps, EVENTS_REFERENCE, READY_SYSTEM_GUIDE and SETUP_PHOTON_PUN2 describe only the legacy stack. ARCHITECTURE, MULTIPLAYER_README and CODE_EXAMPLES mix the legacy stack with MatchmakingManager/NetworkGameController.

title: CardViewManager's manual table selection and drag-to-play paths are unreachable, through to TurnController and Rules51
evidence: Selection: isSelecting is set true only in EnterSelectionMode (CardViewManager 2085-2123), which has no callers. So OnTableCardClicked (1388-1447, subscribed at 1288) always returns at 1392. TryConfirmSelection (2125-2183) and CancelSelection (2185-2204) are reached only from EnterSelectionMode's closures (2114/2119). The fields at 225-231 are used only there, and `view.IsClickable/EnableHover = isSelecting` at 1359-1360 is always false. Drag: CardView.allowDrag is false in code, and no prefab or scene sets `allowDrag: 1`. OnDragReleased is never subscribed (CardViewManager:1583 says so). OnHumanCardDragReleased (1781-1825) is unused. TurnController.OnPlayerDragPlay (2239-2282) is called only from it. Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection (160-226) is called only from these dead paths, and no test uses it. Also never called or never read in CardViewManager: SetCardViewPrefab 19-23, SetTurnController 28-32, GetHandCardScale 126-127, SuitToIndex 234-244, ShowSequentialCaptureHints 1476-1515, and the serialized enableSpriteDebug 132, playSound 143, playSoundVolume 144.
proposed_action: Delete the selection cluster, the drag cluster (CardView OnDragReleased/allowDrag/drag branch of OnMouseDrag 465-490, OnHumanCardDragReleased, TurnController.OnPlayerDragPlay, Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection) and the listed unused members. Keep the OnTableCardClicked subscription only if something else needs the table-card click, otherwise drop it too. That is about 450 lines.
dependencies: Rules51 is in the Project51.Core asmdef, so recompile both assemblies. Run the EditMode tests and play a 1v1 and a 2v2 hand with the capture tray (MoveSelectionUI.ShowInvalid stays: CardViewManager:1928 still uses it).
verdict_reason: The dead paths are real. EnterSelectionMode (2085) has no caller, so isSelecting is never true and OnTableCardClicked returns early. OnHumanCardDragReleased is never subscribed. allowDrag is 0 in Assets/Prefabs/CardView.prefab:105 and has no propertyPath override in any scene/prefab. GetMatchingMovesFromSelection, OnPlayerDragPlay, SetCardViewPrefab, SetTurnController, GetHandCardScale, SuitToIndex, ShowSequentialCaptureHints, enableSpriteDebug, playSound and playSoundVolume have no callers in code, tests (MattaVisualHintsTests reflects only ForceRefresh/StartNewGame/SetupScenarioForCurrentPlayer/ExecuteMove), FindProperty strings or m_MethodName. But one claim is FALSE: 'the fields at 225-231 are used only there'. currentlyHighlightedCards (229) is used by the live capture tray at CardViewManager 2028-2029 and by ClearArrowsAndHighlights 1538-1542. chooserCard (230) is read by OnHumanCardClicked at 1908 and set at 2031. HighlightAlternative (1449) and ClearArrowsAndHighlights (1536) are called from the live tray at 2027/2037/2045/2049. Deleting them as part of the 'selection cluster' breaks the capture tray. The action also leaves more dead code behind.
corrected_action:
Delete only isSelecting, selectionPlayedCard, selectionTableCards and helpShownForCurrentSelection (225-228, 231). KEEP currentlyHighlightedCards, chooserCard, HighlightAlternative and ClearArrowsAndHighlights.

In CardViewManager, delete:

- OnTableCardClicked, together with its subscription at 1288 (table cards are created with IsClickable=false and nothing else uses the click)
- UpdateTableCardsInteractivity (1349), whose only callers are dead
- OnHumanCardDragReleased
- SetCardViewPrefab, SetTurnController, GetHandCardScale and SuitToIndex
- ShowSequentialCaptureHints, and with it StopAllHintAnimations (its only caller)
- the serialized enableSpriteDebug, playSound and playSoundVolume

In CardView, delete the OnDragReleased event, allowDrag, OnMouseDrag, the OnMouseUp drag block (the whole method), dragOffset (set at 248) and isDragging, then simplify its always-false checks (219, 388, 447, 545, 648, 669, 679). Also delete PlayHintBounce, StopHintBounce, HintBounceCoroutine and hintBounceCoroutine, including the cleanup at 714-717; they lose their last caller with ShowSequentialCaptureHints.

Also delete:
- TurnController.OnPlayerDragPlay (2239-2282)
- Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection (159-226, including the orphan '/// <summary>' at 159)
- MoveSelectionUI.ShowMoves (234-244), whose only callers are the deleted CardViewManager 2109/2144 and TurnController 2256.

MoveSelectionUI.ShowInvalid stays (used at CardViewManager 1928). Stale 'allowDrag: 0', 'enableSpriteDebug', 'playSound' and 'playSoundVolume' keys stay harmlessly in CardView.prefab and CardViewManager.prefab until the prefabs are next re-saved.

title: RoundEndPanel is only a forwarder to GamePresentation; its old panel, PlayerScoreRow and the prefab are dead
evidence: RoundEndPanel.Show (line 87) does `if (GamePresentation.ShowRound(...)) return;`. ShowRound returns true whenever a listener exists, and MatchResultsV2 on GamePresentationV2 subscribes in Awake and is always in GameScene. So ShowWithAnimation, CreatePlayerRow, ClearRows, CalculateScoreDetails, ComputePrimieraScore and the ScoreDetails class (91-436, about 340 of 436 lines) never run. Hide() is just GamePresentation.CloseResults(). ScoreDetails and CalculateScoreDetails have no users outside RoundEndPanel/PlayerScoreRow. PlayerScoreRow.cs (317 lines) and Assets/Prefabs/PlayerScoreRow.prefab (guid f74b947e...) are used only by it. GameScene object 'RoundEndPanel' (fileID 2032226892) is active and carries a full old panel (PanelContent, PlayerScoresContainer, ContinueButton, MainMenuButton) that Awake hides.
proposed_action: Make TurnController.ShowRoundEndPanel/OnRoundEndContinue/OnRoundEndMainMenu (2071-2125) call GamePresentation.ShowRound/CloseResults directly with its own callbacks, and drop the roundEndPanel field (line 17). Delete RoundEndPanel.cs, PlayerScoreRow.cs, the prefab and RoundEndPanel_README.md. Remove the RoundEndPanel object from GameScene in the Editor.
dependencies: Block 10 currently keeps RoundEndPanel_README.md; it becomes obsolete. Before deleting, verify in Play mode that the round-end and match-end screens with CONTINUA/menu still work in training and online.
verdict_reason: GamePresentation.ShowRound (Core/GamePresentation.cs:26) returns false only when RoundResults is null. Its only subscriber is MatchResultsV2.Awake (MatchResultsV2.cs:93, unsubscribed in OnDestroy 660). MatchResultsV2 (guid 67a7c7a8) is on the active root object GamePresentationV2 in GameScene (comp 970718487, enabled) and appears in no other scene/prefab. RoundEndPanel.Show therefore always returns at line 87. RoundEndPanel (guid 0cf0fd54) has only one holder: GameScene comp 2032226896 on GameCanvas/RoundEndPanel. The GameScene refs into that 9-object subtree are TurnController.roundEndPanel (line 41525, on GameManager) and GameCanvas's own child list. The subtree has no m_MethodName persistent calls. PlayerScoreRow.cs (guid 21c6b2a5) appears in no YAML. PlayerScoreRow.prefab (f74b947e) is referenced only from GameScene (RoundEndPanel's playerScoreRowPrefab) and by name in RoundEndPanel.cs, PlayerScoreRow.cs and RoundEndPanel_README.md. ScoreDetails, CalculateScoreDetails and RoundEndPanel's ComputePrimieraScore have no outside users; PunteggioManager has its own private copy. Name-based searches find nothing: no 'roundEndPanel' or 'RoundEndPanel' strings in builders, tests, UI51 or UIV2. ShowRoundEndPanel (callers at TurnController 861, 1652, 1824) and OnRoundEndContinue/OnRoundEndMainMenu are not called by reflection or m_MethodName. The proposed TurnController change is equivalent to today's chain (next/menu callbacks, and CloseResults where Hide() was), and keeps the console-log fallback when ShowRound returns false. That fallback is what EditMode tests that AddComponent TurnController already see, because roundEndPanel is null there. RoundEndPanel_README.md is in Block 10's keep list (FASE10_PULIZIA.md:139), as the finding says. Deleting the GameScene object also removes a full-screen transparent Image that Awake disables (SetBlocksInput(false)), which is harmless.

title: AuthBootstrapper's IAuthUI plumbing never runs: authUIComponent is wired to a CanvasScaler
evidence: `[SerializeField] MonoBehaviour authUIComponent` (line 55) is wired in MainMenu to fileID 1564524997, the Canvas_Login CanvasScaler (guid 0cd44c10..., ugui), which does not implement IAuthUI. So the check `authUIComponent is IAuthUI` at 119-121 is never true. RegisterAuthUI (341-358) is called only by LoginGateUI:96, which is dead (Block 3). AuthUIController does not implement IAuthUI. The 27 `_authUI?.` calls are no-ops, and HandleDisplayNameChanged is subscribed only inside RegisterAuthUI. IAuthUI is referenced only by AuthBootstrapper and LoginGateUI.
proposed_action: Delete IAuthUI.cs with LoginGateUI. In AuthBootstrapper, remove authUIComponent, _authUI, RegisterAuthUI, HandleDisplayNameChanged and every `_authUI?.` line. Also drop the unused ShouldShowTapToEnter property (line 74).
dependencies: Do this together with Block 3 (LoginGateUI). Recompile, then test guest entry, login and logout.
verdict_reason: MainMenu.unity:484004 sets authUIComponent: {fileID: 1564524997}. That is a MonoBehaviour with script guid 0cd44c1031e13a943bb63640046fad76 (CanvasScaler) on Canvas_Login, so 'authUIComponent is IAuthUI' at AuthBootstrapper:119 is never true. AuthBootstrapper (guid in MainMenu only) is never added through AddComponent. No FindProperty or SerializedObject access to 'authUIComponent' exists in any builder. IAuthUI is implemented only by LoginGateUI (line 19), and AuthUIController is plain ': MonoBehaviour' (AuthUIController.cs:26). LoginGateUI (guid 92de05a3) and IAuthUI (54742712) have no YAML holders, and no .cs outside these files references them. RegisterAuthUI has one caller, LoginGateUI.cs:96. HandleDisplayNameChanged is subscribed only inside RegisterAuthUI (356-357). Every _authUI use is a null-conditional '?.' call. ShouldShowTapToEnter (line 74) has no references; it is a property, so no m_MethodName can target it. Removing RegisterAuthUI requires deleting LoginGateUI in the same change (Block 3), which the finding states. The lambda 'PlayFabAuth.OnDisplayNameChanged += _ => PublishLook()' at line 116 is separate and must stay. A stale 'authUIComponent:' key will remain in MainMenu YAML, which is harmless.

title: The old PlayerBanner rendering is dead: 4 UI51 banners are wired, and the old children are all inactive
evidence: GameScene PlayerBannerManager: banners[4] = Banner_Local/Left/Top/Right, and ui51Banners[4] = 972075171/552115730/1038711945/422190617, all set. So UI51Banner(relative) is never null, and the old setter block in the refresh loop (117-123: SetName/SetAvatar/SetScore/SetTurnActive/SetScopeCards/SetCapturedPile) never runs. The fallback in SetDealerIndicatorForPlayer (174-175) and GetBannerForPlayer (141-149, used only by that fallback) are dead. The old component's targets are all inactive children of each Banner_*: TurnGlow, ScoreText, ScopeRow, TurnLabel, AvatarFrame, Background, NameText, DealerLabel; only UI51Banner is active. The helpers used only by the dead block are roundedFillSprite (field 23) and CardViewManager.GetCapturedPileDesignOffset (925). The only live use of the old banners is `banner.gameObject.SetActive` on the Banner_* containers.
proposed_action: Change `banners` to the Banner_* RectTransforms (or keep PlayerBanner as an empty marker). Delete the old setter block, GetBannerForPlayer, the dealer fallback, roundedFillSprite and GetCapturedPileDesignOffset. Delete the 8 inactive old children under each Banner_* in the Editor. Delete Scripts/UI/PlayerBanner.cs if nothing else needs it.
dependencies: Hard constraint: keep the Banner_* names (UI51 Fase 5). TurnController reaches SetDealerIndicatorForPlayer by reflection, so keep that method name. TablePlayerBannersBuilder and UIV2FoundationBuilder.Table set these fields (Block 9). Two classes are named PlayerBanner (Project51.Unity.UI and Project51.UI51); removing the old one removes that ambiguity.
verdict_reason: The dead-code claim holds. GameScene.unity:40887-40902 shows PlayerBannerManager.banners = 745376963/464626210/1532830965/1875289147, which are the old PlayerBanner components on Banner_*. ui51Banners = 972075171/552115730/1038711945/422190617, and all four resolve to stripped UI51 PlayerBanner prefab components. UI51Banner(relative) is therefore never null and the old setter block (PlayerBannerManager.cs:117-124) never runs. My subtree scan of each Banner_* found that TurnGlow, ScopeRow, Background, AvatarFrame, NameText, ScoreText, TurnLabel and DealerLabel are all m_IsActive 0, and their only external YAML references come from the old PlayerBanner on the same Banner_* object. No runtime code finds those names (grep for the child-name strings outside Editor hits only PlayerBanner.cs). The Banner_* containers themselves are still live: CardViewManager.cs:838/867 finds them by name, LocalSeatBottomShift lists their RectTransforms, MoveSelectionUI.trayAnchor points at Banner_Local, and GameSocialV2:133 uses only UI51Banner(). GetCapturedPileDesignOffset (CardViewManager.cs:925) has no callers besides line 124; CapturedPileOffsetsBySlot stays in use through TryGetCapturedPileWorldPosition. TurnController.cs:1111-1118 reaches only SetDealerIndicatorForPlayer by reflection. No UnityEvent m_MethodName references any of the removed methods. The finding misses three things. (1) Two Editor files fail to compile once PlayerBanner.cs is gone, not just get re-wired: TablePlayerBannersBuilder.cs:78/119/208 uses `PlayerBanner`, and UIV2FoundationBuilder.Table.cs:77 uses GetComponent<Project51.Unity.UI.PlayerBanner>; Table.cs:59 also does SetPrivateField("roundedFillSprite"). (2) Changing the type of `banners` makes the YAML references to the PlayerBanner MonoBehaviours type-mismatch or dangle. Refresh() then hits `banners[relative] == null -> continue` (line 99) for every seat, so the UI51 banners would silently stop updating names, scores, turn state and scope. That makes re-wiring mandatory. (3) Removing the old components from Banner_* has to happen in the Editor before the script is deleted, otherwise 4 Missing Script components are left behind. A grep of the whole repo (cs/unity/prefab/asset/js, Server included) finds TryGetMoveFromSelection only at its definition, Rules51.cs:116, and at 6 test call sites: Rules51CoreTests 334/350/364, PlayerSelectionTests 19/35, RulesDecisionsTests 30. No reflection string and no m_MethodName hit. GetMatchingMovesFromSelection (Rules51.cs:160) has production callers (CardViewManager 1415/1422/2128/2172, TurnController 2244) and no test. I traced the retarget semantics and they hold. 5-on-5 with selection {5C} returns [CaptureEqual]. 6 vs table {4,5} returns [Capture15]. A fake card or {2,3} when an equal 5 exists returns empty. Empty selection with only PlayOnly valid returns a single new PlayOnly Move (a new instance, but the tests only check Type). The dependency instruction is wrong, though. Rules51.cs is CRLF and non-UTF8, with byte 0x96 at line 96 ('Fisher\x96Yates') and 0xA7 at line 325 ('SPEC \xa710.1'). The Edit tool round-trips the WHOLE file through UTF-8 and would turn both bytes into U+FFFD even though neither line is touched (project memory feedback_non_utf8_source_files, confirmed by hexdump in an earlier session). Git Bash sed -i also converts the CRLF file to LF (memory, Fase 9). 'Edit tool on ASCII-only lines' is therefore not byte-safe. One minor fix: deleting 115-157 leaves two blank lines (114 and 158).
corrected_action: 1) Retarget the 6 call sites to Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection. For acceptance (Rules51CoreTests 334 and 364, PlayerSelectionTests 19): `var m = Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection(...); Assert.AreEqual(1, m.Count); Assert.AreEqual(MoveType.CaptureEqual/PlayOnly/Capture15, m[0].Type);`. For rejection (Rules51CoreTests 350, PlayerSelectionTests 35, RulesDecisionsTests 30): `Assert.IsEmpty(Rules51.GetMatchingMovesFromSelection(...))`. Rename the region and test names to match. These test files are valid UTF-8 (Rules51CoreTests and PlayerSelectionTests are ASCII CRLF; RulesDecisionsTests is LF with valid UTF-8 accents), so the Edit tool is safe on them. Optionally fold PlayerSelectionTests' 2 tests into Rules51CoreTests and delete PlayerSelectionTests.cs and its .meta. 2) Delete Rules51.cs lines 115-158 (the summary line, the function and the trailing blank line). Optionally also drop or complete the dangling `/// <summary>` at 159. Do this with a binary-safe python edit: read 'rb', split on b'\r\n', drop the lines, join with b'\r\n', write 'wb'. Do NOT use the Edit/Write tool (it corrupts the 0x96 byte at line 96 and the 0xA7 byte at line 325) and do NOT use sed -i (it strips CRLF). Then check with `git diff` that only those lines changed, and compare lines 96 and 325 byte-for-byte against HEAD.

proposed_action: Remove the particlesEnabled field, SetParticlesEnabled, and the field's uses at 16, 27 and 126, so that ParticlesEnabled => !GamePreferences.ReducedGraphics. Retarget K6 DisablingParticlesSuppressesPresentationAndClearsSubscribers (103-116) to GamePreferences.SetReducedGraphics(true/false), which keeps the ParticlesDisabled-event assertion, and drop I5:108.
dependencies: tests-explicit-runtime-harness (K6 lines 118-139). GamePreferences and GameFeedback live in Project51.Core.
verdict_reason: The claim holds. grep finds SetParticlesEnabled outside tests only at its definition, GameFeedback.cs:35-40. Callers: K6FeedbackTests 109/113 (in the real test) and 122/135/137 (in RunRuntimeChecks, no caller), and I5ReducedGraphicsTests:108. No reflection string, so `particlesEnabled` is always true at runtime. One line number is off: the reset use is line 127 (126 is `ParticlesDisabled = null;`). The proposed K6 retarget is broken in two ways. (a) K6's FeedbackType() calls GameFeedback.Reset() via reflection, which unsubscribes PolicyChanged and sets policyBound=false. Subscribing to Presented or ParticlesDisabled does not re-bind. So GamePreferences.SetReducedGraphics(true) fires Changed with GameFeedback unbound, ParticlesDisabled never fires, and Assert.AreEqual(1, cleared) fails. The old SetParticlesEnabled called BindPolicy itself. (b) SetReducedGraphics persists Settings_FastAnimations and Settings_GraphicsQuality to PlayerPrefs (GamePreferences.cs:93-97, 82-87), and K6's TearDown restores only Settings_Vibration, so the test would overwrite the developer's Editor graphics preferences. The retargeted test would also duplicate I5.ReducedGraphicsSuppressesNewFeedbackWithoutChangingVibration (103-122), which already saves and restores all four keys.
corrected_action: In GameFeedback.cs (UTF-8 LF, Edit tool safe): delete field 13 and SetParticlesEnabled 35-40. Change line 16 to `get { BindPolicy(); return !GamePreferences.ReducedGraphics; }`, line 27 to `if (GamePreferences.ReducedGraphics) ParticlesDisabled?.Invoke();`, and delete line 127 (`particlesEnabled = true;`). Tests: delete K6FeedbackTests.DisablingParticlesSuppressesPresentationAndClearsSubscribers (102-116) instead of retargeting it. Move its event check into I5.ReducedGraphicsSuppressesNewFeedbackWithoutChangingVibration: replace line 108 with `_ = GameFeedback.ParticlesEnabled;` (which forces BindPolicy, since static binding state depends on earlier tests), subscribe a `cleared++` handler to GameFeedback.ParticlesDisabled, assert cleared == 1 after SetReduced(true), and unsubscribe it in the finally block. That test's SetUp/TearDown already restores the PlayerPrefs. K6 RunRuntimeChecks (122/135/137) must either be deleted (tests-explicit-runtime-harness) or switched to SetReduced plus a preference restore. Update docs/ui/k6-feedback-plan.md:20.

Everything in a Resources folder is always in the build. Its 5 sprite fields (PanelGlass fa0b8f04..., ButtonPrimary e22f8e2a..., ButtonSecondary 15556c12..., GlowSoft 628a107e..., DropShadow a14eab0e...) point to GUIDs that exist nowhere in Assets.
Referencers:
- Prefabs: HomePanel, JoinRoomPopup, PlayerSlot, WaitingRoomPanel.
- MainMenu: Canvas_Dynamic/SafeArea/<MainHud> and OnlineFlowV2/LegacyOnlineViews/MatchmakingStatusUI(+CancelButton).
- Editor only: the block-1 builders (ThemePath const) and LobbyPrefabBuilder/DragonsHoardThemeApplier via Resources.Load<UITheme>.
No runtime Resources.Load of it.
proposed_action: Delete it after blocks 1, 5 and 7 have removed its referencers. The UITheme script goes with it if no other users remain (code area).
dependencies: Blocks 1 (HomeScreen builders), 5 (LegacyOnlineViews, LobbyPrefabBuilder), 7 (MainHud).
verdict_reason: Assets/Resources/DragonsHoardTheme.asset (guid 132b545538ac65e4e878b64ed6fe819e, script UITheme 7315332b...). None of its 5 sprite GUIDs (fa0b8f04, e22f8e2a, 15556c12, 628a107e, a14eab0e) is in any .meta under Assets, Packages or Library/PackageCache, so all 5 refs are broken. A GUID grep over all .unity/.prefab/.asset/.mat/.cs files finds only these referencers: HomePanel.prefab (nested in MainHud.prefab), JoinRoomPopup.prefab, PlayerSlot.prefab (nested in WaitingRoomPanel), WaitingRoomPanel.prefab, and MainMenu.unity with 4 refs. Resolved via YAML, the 4 MainMenu refs are 2 ThemedButton components added on the MainHud prefab instance (PrefabInstance 3378492087178908962, source MainHud.prefab), the ThemedPanel on OnlineFlowV2/LegacyOnlineViews/MatchmakingStatusUI[off] and the ThemedButton on its CancelButton. No ref in GameScene, HomeScreen.unity or Tests. Code: only Editor builders. Block 1 uses ThemePath + AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath (Amici, Classifica, DeckPage, EmoticonScreenExact, HomeScreen, Impostazioni, Negozio, PanelMazzo, PanelModalita, Posta, Premi, Profilo). DragonsHoardThemeApplier (block 1) and LobbyPrefabBuilder (block 5) use Resources.Load<UITheme>("DragonsHoardTheme"). There is no runtime Resources.Load. The ThemedButton/ThemedPanel script GUIDs appear only on the same referencers, so after blocks 1, 5 and 7 remove them, UITheme.cs, ThemedButton.cs and ThemedPanel.cs all lose their last users. Deleting the asset before that would only make ThemedButton.OnEnable log warnings. The dependencies are complete. If block 7b (keep MainHud) is chosen, the asset has to stay.

title: Old DragonsHoard emoticon PNGs (6 files, 6.3 MB): only dead builders reference them
evidence:
0 GUID referencers, not in the build (1774x887 each). Builders that name them:
- DeckPageBuilder and EmoticonScreenExactBuilder (block 1).
- UIV2SandboxSceneBuilder (block 2).
- FrontendExpansionBuilder(.Game) (blocks 4/9). These actually load sprites from 14_emoticon_set.png, which was already deleted on 27/09.
The live emoticons are UI51/Art/Emoticons/*_sheet_8frames.png (UI51EmoticonSet) plus the UIV2 sheets (see assets-uiv2-emoticons-dup).
proposed_action: Delete the 6 PNGs together with the block 1/2 builders.
dependencies: Blocks 1 and 2 builders, which would otherwise log missing sprites if run.
verdict_reason: There are indeed 0 GUID referencers and the files are not in the build, but the evidence misses the real consumer. UIV2FoundationBuilder.AnimatedEmoticons.cs ('Tools/UIV2/Build Animated Emoticons') reads exactly these files as its 4x2 8-frame source sheets: SheetsDir + '/emo_<name>.png' via File.Exists/File.ReadAllBytes at lines 44-46. SheetsDir is this DragonsHoard folder (UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs:30). From them it generates Assets/UIV2/Art/Emoticons/emo_*_anim.png, the emo_*.anim files and Emoticons.controller, and these are live. Every emo_*_anim.png is referenced by GameScene.unity and MainMenu.unity, emo_risata_anim.png also by UI51/Prefabs/Collection_EmoticonCard.prefab, and Emoticons.controller by GameScene. GameSocialV2.cs:198-202 plays state 'E'+index. So these 6 PNGs are the only source art of live generated sheets. They are not copies of the UI51 sheets: those are 1024x512 and differ (mean pixel diff about 22 after resize). The finder's other claims hold: FrontendExpansionBuilder.cs:54/.Game.cs:21, UIV2SandboxSceneBuilder and UIV2FoundationBuilder.Collection.cs:358/477 load 'emo_*' from the deleted 14_emoticon_set.png. DeckPageBuilder and EmoticonScreenExactBuilder (block 1) look the files up by name. Risk if the PNGs go before AnimatedEmoticons.cs: rerunning that menu first calls AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset on Emoticons.controller and recreates it with only the 'Static' state (every source fails File.Exists). The table emoticons would then silently stop animating, because GameSocialV2 falls back when HasState is false. SPRINT_BACKLOG.md:814 already marks that menu as 'do not rerun'.
corrected_action: User decision. Prefer moving the 6 PNGs out of Assets as source art (e.g. Design/source/emoticons) over deleting them, because they are the only originals of the live Assets/UIV2/Art/Emoticons/emo_*_anim.png (and of the generated .anim files and Emoticons.controller). Do it in the same change that deletes UIV2FoundationBuilder.AnimatedEmoticons.cs (block 9), never before. Also remove UIV2FoundationBuilder.Collection.cs (block 9), UIV2SandboxSceneBuilder (block 2), DeckPageBuilder/EmoticonScreenExactBuilder (block 1) and FrontendExpansionBuilder(.Game) (blocks 4/9). The import_manifest.json entries for emo_* go with assets-dh-import-manifest. Do not touch Assets/UIV2/Art/Emoticons/* unless assets-uiv2-emoticons-dup first moves GameScene, MainMenu and Collection_EmoticonCard.prefab off them.

title: Delete 14 non-cream + 3 unused cream standalone DragonsHoard icons (12.5 MB); correction to prior 'keep ic_*'
evidence:
All 17 have 0 GUID referencers and none is in the build. How each kind of builder finds icons:
- UI51 builders look up sprites by name only in Assets/UI51/Art/<area>/<name>.png (UI51Build.Sprite, UI51Build.cs:35-41), never in DragonsHoard. So block 11's 'ic_* are looked up by name by UI51 builders' is wrong for this folder.
- UIV2 NewIcon() maps every name through CreamIcons (UIV2FoundationBuilder.IconSetV2.cs:27-38), so no builder loads the non-cream files.
- The kept builders' 'ic_lock', 'ic_person', 'ic_trophy' and 'ic_chest' are sprite names inside the Icons.png sheet (LoadSprite(IconsPath,...); Icons.png.meta contains ic_lock, ic_person, ic_trophy...).
- ic_bot_cream, ic_question_cream and ic_volume_cream are only targets of the IconSetV2 list. UI51 has its own ic_bot_cream in Art/Common.
- ic_arrow_left, ic_fulmine and ic_remove: no code at all.
- The remaining file-name lookups are the block-1 builders via DragonsHoardSprites (FindAssets name search).
proposed_action: Delete the 17 PNGs. Keep the cream icons that are still referenced (ic_accuso/cards/chat/check/chest/close/copy/exit/globe/home/link/lock/nav_back/paste/person/settings/share/trophy/warn _cream, ic_mail): see assets-dh-ui51-duplicates.
dependencies: Do it together with or after block 1 (DragonsHoardSprites name search) and block 9 (IconSetV2 list), otherwise 'Tools/UIV2/Apply Icon Set v2' logs 3 missing files. Code-area note: block 9 cannot delete UIV2FoundationBuilder.IconSetV2.cs as-is, because the kept main partial UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs calls NewIcon() (lines 547, 1551, 1556), which is defined there.
verdict_reason: The conclusion holds. All 17 have 0 GUID referencers and are not in the build. UI51Build.Sprite only loads Assets/UI51/Art/<area>/<name>.png (UI51Build.cs:34-40); UI51 has its own Common/ic_bot_cream.png; no UI51 code mentions DragonsHoard. Every kept-builder 'ic_lock', 'ic_person', 'ic_trophy' or 'ic_gear' is a sub-sprite of Icons.png (Icons.png.meta names include ic_lock, ic_person, ic_trophy, ic_x, ic_gear, ic_warn): StartScreenAuthButtonsBuilder.IconSprite reads only Icons.png, and LoadSprite(IconsPath, ...) likewise. No kept NewIcon caller (UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs: ic_chest, ic_mail, ic_trophy) maps to a deleted file. Two evidence claims are false, though. (1) 'ic_arrow_left: no code at all' is wrong: IconSetV2.cs:87 does LoadSprite(SheetsDir + "/ic_arrow_left.png", "ic_arrow_left") as a key of the swap Dictionary. (2) 'No builder loads the non-cream files' is wrong: IconSetV2.cs:94-97 loads SheetsDir/<gold>.png for every CreamIcons key, which covers ic_chest, ic_trophy, ic_exit, ic_arrowback, ic_X, ic_option, ic_volume, ic_questionmark, ic_share, ic_lock and ic_person. Both sit inside ApplyIconSetV2. The consequence is also understated: without ic_volume_cream, ApplyIconSetV2 throws a NullReferenceException at line 66 (AssetImporter.GetAtPath returns null for the first missing file) instead of 'logging 3 missing files'. Without ic_arrow_left, LoadSprite returns null and the Dictionary initializer throws ArgumentNullException. Other name searches are unaffected because Icons.png carries the same names: TableActionButtonsBuilder and TableTopBarBuilder (FindAssets t:Sprite in Assets/UI/Sprites), and DragonsHoardSprites, which only indexes Multiple-mode sheets. The finder's block-9 note is correct: UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs calls NewIcon at lines 547, 1551 and 1556. Online.cs and Table.cs (block 9) also use the IconSetV2 array, and Online.cs defines VisiblePadding, which FitVisible uses.
corrected_action: Delete the 17 PNGs (13.1 MB) in the same change that removes the 'Tools/UIV2/Apply Icon Set v2' menu: in UIV2FoundationBuilder.IconSetV2.cs, delete ApplyIconSetV2, SwapSprites, FitVisible, VisibleRect, PathIcons and the IconSetV2 array. Move NewIcon, IconFile and CreamIcons into the kept UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs, and drop the now-dead CreamIcons entries ic_volume, ic_questionmark and ic_bot. Only remove the IconSetV2 array if UIV2FoundationBuilder.Online.cs and .Table.cs are deleted in the same block 9 step; otherwise they stop compiling. Block 1 (DragonsHoardSprites and its builders) must be gone or never rerun. Keep the referenced cream set and ic_mail exactly as the finder listed.

title: 4 oversized sprites fill most of the UI51_Common atlas; ribbon_gray likely does not fit and ships uncompressed
evidence:
Sizes against how each sprite is shown:
- crown_gold.png is 1254x1254 but drawn at 40x37 design px (UI51ResultsBuilder.cs:273).
- ribbon_gray.png is 2172x724. It is swapped with ribbon.png (256x98) in the same 84-px TopBand Image (UI51ResultsBuilder.cs:247, UI51ResultsView.cs:341). Neither has a 9-slice border, and no SetNativeSize exists anywhere in the runtime code.
- rays_conic is 1254 at 420 design px and 16% alpha.
- Sun_fix is 1278x1230 (62 px emblem plus the table felt emblem).
These 4 are 6.3M of the 8.75M px in the Common folder, which already exceeds 2 full 2048x2048 pages. ribbon_gray is imported at max 2048, so 2048x682 plus padding 4 exceeds the atlas max 2048. It is probably left unpacked and, because UI51ImportBuilder.ApplyCommon (line 97) sets atlas sources to Uncompressed, ships as RGBA32 (about 5.3 MB). This last point is PLAUSIBLE: check it in the Sprite Atlas preview.
proposed_action: Downscale the source PNGs: crown_gold to 256x256, ribbon_gray to 512x171 (same aspect). Optionally take rays_conic to 640 and Sun_fix to 512 after a Simulator check of the results screen and the table emblem. Then run Tools/UI51/Import Settings + Atlases and verify UI51_Common page count in the atlas preview. Rects are fixed by the builders, so the layout does not change.
dependencies: Re-run the UI51 import/atlas menu. Visual check of Fine partita (crown, gray ribbon on defeat) and the table emblem with ui-verify.
verdict_reason:
Sizes are confirmed: crown_gold 1254x1254, ribbon_gray 2172x724, rays_conic 1254x1254, Sun_fix 1278x1230. Together they are 6.29M of the 8.75M px in Common. All have max 2048, no platform override, and default compression Uncompressed (ApplyCommon line 97). The 02/10 Android build report shows UI51_Common.spriteatlasv2 at 5.4 mb, about three 2048 ASTC 6x6 pages, so the oversize problem is real. The claim that ribbon_gray is unpacked and ships as RGBA32 (~5.3 MB) is REFUTED by the same report: ribbon_gray.png is listed at only 14.7 kb (sprite object), so its texture is inside the atlas. The proposed sizes are partly too small for the display:
- ribbon_gray fills TopBand(Title,0,0,16,84) in a 260-wide parent (UI51ResultsBuilder.cs:243-247): 260x84 design, about 780x252 device px on 3x phones. 512x171 would be upscaled 1.5x.
- Sun_fix is also the table felt emblem. TableFeltRenderer.UpdateEmblem sizes it at 220/370 of the table width, about 220 design px or 660 device px. 512 would be upscaled.
- crown_gold is drawn at 40x37 design (about 120 device px), so 256 is fine.
- rays_conic is drawn at 420/440 design at 16% alpha. 640-768 is acceptable after a check.
These four sources have no copy in Design/ (only git), and Sun_fix is the user's own art (SPRINT_BACKLOG.md:735), so downscaling in place destroys the masters. An importer max-size override alone is not durable: UI51ImportBuilder.ApplyCommon line 94 resets maxTextureSize to 2048 on every Tools/UI51/Import Settings + Atlases run.
corrected_action:
This is the user's call.
1. Copy the four originals outside Assets first (e.g. Design/ui51_sources/).
2. Downscale the Assets copies to on-device display size: crown_gold 256x256, ribbon_gray 1024x341 (not 512), Sun_fix about 768x739 (not 512), rays_conic about 768.
3. Run Tools/UI51/Import Settings + Atlases and check the UI51_Common page count in the atlas preview (expect 2 pages instead of 3, about 1.8 MB less in the build).
4. Run ui-verify on Fine partita (crown, gray ribbon on defeat), LivelloSu (rays, MainMenu), the Sorteggio emblem and the table felt emblem.
Drop the 'ribbon_gray ships uncompressed' claim. If the masters must stay at full resolution in Assets instead, the only durable route is a per-file max size in UI51ImportBuilder.ApplyCommon (a code change).

evidence:

verdict_reason:
The duplicate pairs exist, but the action is wrong or overstated in several places.
(1) The quick win reverses a documented choice. UIV2FoundationBuilder.HomeAmbient.cs:79 reads ShrinkForUi("home_bg_base", 4096, false) with the comment "a 2048 tornerebbe sotto la risoluzione degli iPhone". HomeAmbient is a builder block 9 keeps, so it resets 4096 on every run. DH home_bg_base (1882x3344, Default max 4096, no overrides) is the live full-screen Home background (MainMenu HomeAmbient/Region/AboveNav/Frame/BG_Base, its only reference). Capping it at 2048 gives 1153x2048, a visible softening on high-res phones, so user_visible=false is wrong.
(2) The logo swap is visible. StartScreenV2/DesignArea/Logo is 670x670 units with preserveAspect. The DH logo is 1234x1197; the UI51 logo is 512x497, so it would be upscaled about 1.3-1.6x.
(3) The icon savings are small. All DH cream icons and DH ic_mail already import at Default max 256 (set by IconSetV2), the same as the 256 px UI51 copies, so each is about 64 KB.
(4) Most DH refs sit under inactive subtrees that blocks 4-7 delete anyway: QuickDeckV2/QuickModeV2/SettingsV2 PanelFrame(off), OnlineFlowV2 panels(off), DeleteAccountV2/LegalV2(off), Login/RegisterPanel Design(off), and SettingsQuickAction under HomeScreenV2[INACTIVE]. Others are Icon(off) children that the UI51 builder hides: TableActionButtons EmojiButton/Icon(off) and AccusoButton/Icon(off) (the only user of ic_accuso_cream), and TableTopBar/SettingsButton(off).
(5) The finder's live list misses refs inside UIV2 prefab assets that MainMenu instances: HomeScreenV2.prefab (ic_mail, chest, trophy), UIV2_BottomNav (home, cards, person), ProfileScreenV2 (settings), plus item prefabs those screens reference (DeckCard, EmoticonCard, AccusoRow, ShopDeckCard, ProfileTrophyTile, UIV2_AvatarBadge, UIV2_IconButton, UIV2_CollectionCard).
(6) Kept code still loads from DH: UIV2FoundationBuilder.cs:1561 NewIcon("ic_mail") through the IconSetV2 map.
(7) DH ic_bot_cream, ic_question_cream and ic_volume_cream have 0 references, so they are not in the build. question and volume also lack UI51 twins, not only accuso.
corrected_action:
Leave DH home_bg_base (4096) and DH logo_51 on StartScreenV2 as they are. If the user still wants the 2048 cap, present it as a visible trade-off and also change HomeAmbient.cs:79 to 2048, or the builder reverts it.
Run the consolidation only after blocks 4-7, when most DH refs are already gone with their subtrees:

Only then delete the DH copies with 0 references. ic_bot/question/volume_cream can go as soon as IconSetV2 (block 9) is gone.

title: Glow/blur textures imported at full 1254/1672 px (one with mipmaps)
evidence:
Import settings:
- Bagliore morbido cerchio: 1254x1254, max 2048, enableMipMap 1. Used by CardViewManager.prefab, HomeMotes, StartMotes and legacy MatchResults.
- Bagliore morbido rettangolo: 1254 (DealerAccusoReveal/Window/Glow plus legacy).
- Bagliore morbido: 1254 (AccusoImpact/Visual/Burst).
- Sfocatura sfondo: 941x1672 (InGameSettings/Panel/Veil plus legacy veils).
All are soft glows or blurs. The UI51 handoff ships the same glow at 512 (UI51/Art/Common/Bagliore_morbido.png) and its full-screen blur at 540x959 (UI51/Art/Backgrounds/home_bg_blur.png).
proposed_action: Android/iPhone overrides: maxTextureSize 512 for the three Bagliore textures and 1024 for Sfocatura sfondo. Expected saving: about 5 MB of RAM and build (ETC2-equivalent), with no visible difference on blurred content. Leave mipmaps on 'cerchio' only if the world-space card glow shimmers without them.
dependencies: Quick Simulator check of Home motes, card glow and the dealer accuso window.
verdict_reason:
The import settings check out. All four are 1254x1254 (Sfocatura 941x1672) at Default max 2048 with no Android/iPhone overrides. Only 'cerchio' has mipmaps; it has a 9-slice border of 626. 'rettangolo' has a 9-slice border of (336,528,361,517). Unity scales the sprite border and PPU with the platform max size, so sliced and world-space uses keep their size. CardView halo sizing also normalises by sprite bounds.
Users found:
- cerchio: a GameScene override of mattaHaloSprite and moveHintGlowSprite on the CardViewManager.prefab instance (the prefab asset itself has no reference), HomeMotes and StartScreenV2/StartMotes (MainMenu), plus legacy MatchResults motes and TableActionButtons/AccusoWindowGlow(off).
- rettangolo: DealerAccusoReveal/Window/Glow plus legacy.
- 'Bagliore morbido': AccusoImpact/Visual/Burst.
- Sfocatura: only inactive or hidden veils. DealerRoulette/Veil is hidden by legacyOnly whenever playerCount is 2 or 4 (DealerRouletteController:100-102). InGameSettings/Panel(off)/Veil(off) and RoundResults(off)/Veil(off) are never enabled by code. So Sfocatura is never actually shown.
The error is the mipmap remark. UIV2FoundationBuilder.Motes.cs:74-82 (EnsureCircleGlowMipmaps) documents that without mipmaps the motes at 20-50 px flicker and turn grey. Even at 512 the downscale is 10-25x, and that kept builder re-enables mipmaps anyway. The ~5 MB saving estimate is right (about 6.3 MB down to about 1.4 MB at 1 B/px).
corrected_action:
Add Android and iPhone overrides:
- maxTextureSize 512 for 'Bagliore morbido cerchio', 'Bagliore morbido rettangolo' and 'Bagliore morbido'. Keep enableMipMap=1 on 'cerchio' unconditionally (Motes.cs documents why).
- maxTextureSize 1024 for 'Sfocatura sfondo'. It is never displayed, so its refs can also simply go when blocks 4-7 remove the legacy veils.
If assets-dh-ui51-duplicates swaps the AccusoImpact Burst to UI51 Bagliore_morbido, skip the override on 'Bagliore morbido'.
Check in the Simulator: Home/Start motes, matta halo, move-hint card glow, and the dealer accuso window glow.

title: Home ambient overlay layers are full-canvas 941x1672 but only 3-29% visible
evidence: Alpha bounding boxes (alpha>8): shooting_star 294x160 (3%), castle_lights 520x322 (11%), stars 611x640 (25%), bushes 941x474 (28%), torch_glow 941x479 (29%). All are live on the Home screen (<UIV2_Home>/HomeAmbient/Region/AboveNav/Frame/*) and imported as 941x1672 (about 1.5 MB each in ETC2 terms, 7.5 MB total).
proposed_action: Crop each PNG to its alpha bbox and place it with anchors/offsets in the HomeAmbient builder, keeping the same visual position (lossless). This cuts their texture memory by about 75%.
dependencies: Change the UIV2FoundationBuilder.HomeAmbient layout math, then pixel-compare the Home before and after (ui-verify).
verdict_reason:
Verified:
- All five layers are 941x1672 at Default max 2048, and each has one MainMenu reference (torch_glow has 2: the RawImage halves).
- The alpha>8 bboxes match the finder: shooting_star 294x160, castle_lights 520x322, stars 611x640, bushes 941x474, torch_glow 941x479. That is 1.50 MP of 7.87 MP.
- Placement comes from UIV2FoundationBuilder.HomeAmbient.cs (OverlayImage/PlaceInArt; CastleLights uses Place = (79,35, 0.875W, 0.925H); TorchGlow uses RawImage uvRect halves with a pivot computed from TorchGlowCentres y=688 on the full-height layer).
- No tests or runtime lookups depend on the sizes.
The 'lossless' claim is not exact at alpha>8. Faint pixels outside that box are cut: torch_glow has 42385 px with alpha up to 8, castle_lights 3208, bushes 1522. Cropping at alpha>1 gives 1.64 MP, almost the same ~79% saving, and drops only alpha-1 noise. alpha>0 would keep 5.33 MP.
The PNGs are the user's DragonsHoard art, so cropping in place changes source art (git keeps the originals); user_decision=true is correct.
corrected_action:
1. Crop the five PNGs at the alpha>1 bbox with 2 px transparent padding, so bilinear filtering does not clamp at the edge.
2. In UIV2FoundationBuilder.HomeAmbient.cs, give Stars, ShootingStar and Bushes a Place equal to their bbox in 941x1672 art pixels. Set CastleLights Place to (79 + bx*0.875, 35 + by*0.925, bw*0.875, bh*0.925).
3. For TorchGlow, keep the uvRect x-halves. Place each half at (side*half, by, half, bh) and compute its pivot from TorchGlowCentres relative to the cropped rect (y offset 407).
4. Re-run Tools/UIV2/Build Home Ambient. It forces MainMenu open, rebuilds HomeAmbient and re-wires HomeV2Integration.homeAmbient.
5. Pixel-compare the Home before and after in the Simulator (ui-verify).
The unreferenced home_vines and home_flame_b are a separate item.

title: Library/PackageCache is tracked in git (3834 files, 46.6 MB) even though .gitignore ignores /Library/
evidence: `git ls-files Library` = 3834 files, all under Library/PackageCache (visualscripting 1596, collab-proxy 581, timeline 352, 2d.animation 283, test-framework 278, ...). `git ls-tree -r -l HEAD Library` sums to 46.6 MB. They were all added in one commit, 445db61 (2025-12-10, 'update version 0.001'), and none has changed since. `git check-ignore` confirms .gitignore line 6 `/[Ll]ibrary/` matches these paths, so they are tracked only because they were added before the rule existed.
proposed_action: `git rm -r --cached Library` (the files stay on disk; Unity owns them) and commit. No .gitignore change is needed.
dependencies: None. ParrelSync clones use their own Library.
verdict_reason: The facts check out. `git ls-files Library` returns 3834 files, all under Library/PackageCache, and they total 46.59 MB in HEAD. All of them come from one commit, 445db61 (2025-12-10). .gitignore line 6 `/[Ll]ibrary/` matches them (check-ignore). `git status --short Library` is clean, so there are no local edits to lose. Only a subset is tracked: mostly .cs, .asmdef, .uss, .uxml and .dll, with no .meta files. For example visualscripting has 1596 tracked files out of 3853 on disk, and textmeshpro 109 out of 324. Every package comes from a registry or git URL in Packages/manifest.json, so the cache can be rebuilt. ParrelSync clones (../51_clone_0, ../51_clone_1) are not git working trees; their Assets/ is a symlink and they have their own Library, so that part of the claim holds. What the finder missed: `main`, `backup/pre-fase2-local` and the remote codex/* branches still track these files. After the commit, `git checkout main` (or any older commit) followed by a checkout back to the cleaned branch makes git delete the 3834 files from Library/PackageCache on disk, because they are tracked in one commit and absent from the other. Any other clone that pulls the commit loses them the same way. That leaves partial package folders (TMP, test-framework, timeline...) until Unity rebuilds the cache. So 'Dependencies: None' is incomplete.
corrected_action: Run `git rm -r --cached Library` and commit; no .gitignore change. Dependencies to add: (1) merge the commit into main promptly, so no tracked branch still carries Library/PackageCache. (2) Until then, do not check out main or older commits while Unity is open. If a checkout or pull removes files from Library/PackageCache, close Unity, delete Library/PackageCache and reopen so the Package Manager re-resolves. (3) Do this before or in the same commit as hyg-pkg-visualscripting. Otherwise removing that package shows up as 1596 tracked deletions under Library/PackageCache/com.unity.visualscripting@1.9.4.

title: NetworkGameController duplicates the card wire format of Core GameStateSerializer
evidence: NetworkGameController.SerializeMove/DeserializeMove (~813-878) re-implement the comma-separated 'Suit:Rank' card list that already exists in GameStateSerializer.SerializeCards/DeserializeCards (~121-137). SerializeGameState/DeserializeGameState (~639-655) are one-line wrappers. There is an empty '#region RPC Methods'.
proposed_action: Move SerializeMove/DeserializeMove into GameStateSerializer, reusing SerializeCards/DeserializeCards. Keep the exact wire format: PlayerIndex|Suit:Rank|(int)Type, plus '|cards' only when non-empty. Inline the 2 wrappers and drop the empty region. Add one round-trip EditMode test.
dependencies: The wire format must stay byte-identical. Since 2.32 only same-version builds match, but a mismatch would still break the move replay on rejoin (2.59). Run NetworkAccusoSyncTests and an online smoke test.
verdict_reason:
The duplication is real. NetworkGameController.SerializeMove (lines 813-830) builds the 'Suit:Rank' list joined by ',' exactly as GameStateSerializer.SerializeCards does (lines 121-125). DeserializeMove (834-878) parses it like DeserializeCards (127-138). Move (Core/Move.cs) and GameStateSerializer both live in Project51.Core. The only call sites are line 593 (SendMove) and line 675 (RPC_ExecuteMove).

Two parts of the evidence are wrong:
- '#region RPC Methods' (line 659) is NOT empty. It holds RPC_ExecuteMove and the other RPCs through line 805, and all regions are balanced (Reconnection is nested in Unity Lifecycle).
- DeserializeGameState is not a one-line wrapper. It wraps GameStateSerializer.Deserialize in try/catch with an error log and returns null, and its caller at line 756 relies on that null. Inlining it as-is would let a malformed payload throw inside the Photon RPC.

The wire format can stay byte-identical: SerializeCards returns '' for empty, and the move appends '|cards' only when Count > 0. DeserializeMove's try/catch-to-null behaviour must also be kept.
corrected_action:
Add GameStateSerializer.SerializeMove(Move) and TryDeserializeMove(string), or a DeserializeMove that returns null on malformed input. Both reuse SerializeCards/DeserializeCards and keep the format PlayerIndex|Suit:Rank|(int)Type plus '|cards' only when CapturedCards is non-empty. TurnId and Timeout stay as separate RPC arguments.

Call them at NetworkGameController lines 593 and 675, and delete the Serialization region (lines 807-880).

Optionally inline only SerializeGameState (2 call sites, lines 562 and 630). Keep DeserializeGameState, or move its try/catch into a GameStateSerializer.TryDeserialize used at line 756.

Do not touch '#region RPC Methods'.

Add one EditMode test that asserts an exact string (for example '0|Denari:7|1|Coppe:3,Spade:4'), an empty-capture string without a trailing '|', and a round trip. Run NetworkAccusoSyncTests and an online smoke test.

title: TurnController repeats the same NetworkGameController reflection lookup 3 times
evidence: Three near-identical blocks resolve 'Project51.Networking.NetworkGameController, Assembly-CSharp', call FindObjectOfType on it and then GetMethod: ~676-688 (SendInitialGameState), ~1416-1437 (SendInitialGameState/RequestResync) and ~2047-2057 (SendAccuso). Reflection is required because the Gameplay asmdef cannot reference Assembly-CSharp (memory: assembly boundaries).
proposed_action: Add one private helper, bool TryInvokeNetwork(string method, params object[] args), that caches the Type and instance, and replace the 3 blocks. Keep the method-name strings unchanged.
dependencies: The method names in NetworkGameController must not be renamed (they are string-bound).
verdict_reason: The three duplicated blocks are real: Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/TurnController.cs lines 676-687 (StartNewGame, SendInitialGameState), 1416-1437 (RequestNetworkResync, SendInitialGameState/RequestResync) and 2047-2057 (TrySendAccusoSync, SendAccuso). All three resolve 'Project51.Networking.NetworkGameController, Assembly-CSharp'. Reflection is required: NetworkGameController lives in Assets/Scripts/Networking, which has no asmdef (it is in Assembly-CSharp), and Gameplay is the Project51.Gameplay asmdef. The finder's evidence is wrong in one detail. The blocks do NOT call FindObjectOfType. They read the static property NetworkGameController.Instance through GetProperty('Instance'), and that property (NetworkGameController.cs:20-30) does its own lazy FindObjectOfType and keeps its own Unity-null-aware cache. The proposed helper must NOT cache the instance in TurnController. Through reflection it is held as a plain 'object', so '!= null' compares references and skips Unity's lifetime check. If the NetworkGameController is destroyed (it has OnDestroy and no DontDestroyOnLoad), the stale reference would still be invoked, and its Photon calls would throw MissingReferenceException. The method names SendInitialGameState(GameState), RequestResync() and SendAccuso(int,int) at NetworkGameController.cs:616/511/35 are string-bound. No test references them.
corrected_action: Add one private static helper to TurnController, e.g. 'static bool InvokeNetwork(string method, params object[] args)'. It caches only System.Type (and optionally the PropertyInfo 'Instance'), reads Instance on EVERY call, returns false if the type or instance is null, and otherwise calls GetMethod(method, Public|Instance)?.Invoke(instance, args). Replace the 3 blocks: the master-send at 676-687 keeps its Debug.Log when the call succeeds; RequestNetworkResync keeps its isMaster branch (InvokeNetwork("SendInitialGameState", gameState) or InvokeNetwork("RequestResync")); TrySendAccusoSync calls InvokeNetwork("SendAccuso", playerIndex, (int)type). Do not cache the NetworkGameController instance. Keep the method-name strings unchanged and do not rename those 3 public methods in NetworkGameController.cs. Leave SetDealerIndicatorViaReflection (PlayerBannerManager, line 1109) as it is: a different type and lookup. TurnController.cs is UTF-8 with LF line endings and contains non-ASCII characters, so use the Edit tool. Then run the EditMode tests and a 2-client online smoke test (initial state, accuso, resync).

title: Pointless reflection for CameraResponsiveFit inside its own assembly
evidence: GameSceneInitializer (~493-507) and CardViewManager (~660-667) look it up by string: GetComponent('CameraResponsiveFit'), Type.GetType('Project51.Unity.CameraResponsiveFit, Project51.Gameplay') and GetMethod('Apply'). CameraResponsiveFit.cs (public void Apply() at line 47) is in the same Gameplay assembly as both callers.
proposed_action: Replace with GetComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>() ?? AddComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>() and fit.Apply().
dependencies: None. Tests reflect 'targetCamera' on some type, so check that the field name is kept.
verdict_reason: The problem is real. CameraResponsiveFit (Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/CameraResponsiveFit.cs, namespace Project51.Unity, public void Apply() at line 47) is in the same Project51.Gameplay asmdef and namespace as GameSceneInitializer.cs (EnsureResponsiveCamera, 493-507) and CardViewManager.cs (ApplyResponsiveCameraIfAvailable, 660-667). CardViewManager already references the type directly at line 65 (CameraResponsiveFit.DesignWorldHeight). The only test hit for 'targetCamera' is K5TableTests.cs:148, which reflects TableFeltRenderer.targetCamera; in GameSceneInitializer it is just a local variable, so nothing breaks. GameScene.unity holds one CameraResponsiveFit instance (GUID f684879f...), so the AddComponent path is only a fallback. Two parts of the proposed action are wrong. (1) 'GetComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>() ?? AddComponent<...>()' is unsafe on UnityEngine.Object. In the Editor, GetComponent<T> returns a fake-null object when the component is missing, and '??' skips Unity's == override. AddComponent would then never run in Play Mode in the Editor, and fit.Apply() would throw MissingComponentException. (2) CardViewManager never adds the component; it only applies one that is already there. Applying the same GetComponent-or-AddComponent there would change its behaviour.
corrected_action: GameSceneInitializer.EnsureResponsiveCamera: replace lines 493-507 with 'var fit = targetCamera.GetComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>(); if (fit == null) fit = targetCamera.gameObject.AddComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>(); fit.Apply();'. This drops the Type.GetType branch and its 'type not available yet' warning. CardViewManager.ApplyResponsiveCameraIfAvailable: replace lines 660-667 with 'var fit = layoutCamera.GetComponent<CameraResponsiveFit>(); if (fit != null) fit.Apply();'. Keep the apply-only-if-present behaviour, without AddComponent. Do not use '??' or '?.' on Unity objects. Both files are UTF-8 with CRLF line endings and contain non-ASCII characters, so use the Edit tool. Nothing else depends on this.

title: ProfileService: dead client stat writes (contradict server-only stats), dead profile/nickname/deck/title members, unused Trophies stat

title: PhotonAuthConnector only reports auth-cause disconnects: a network drop during the first connect waits out the 30 s timeout. Its disconnect events and nickname API are unused
evidence: OnDisconnected raises OnConnectionFailed only for InvalidAuthentication, CustomAuthenticationFailed and AuthenticationTicketExpired. Any other cause (ExceptionOnConnect, DnsExceptionOnConnect, ServerTimeout, ...) during the initial connect raises nothing, so AuthBootstrapper sits on its own 30 s wait. Two separate 30 s timeouts exist: the connector's Update and AuthBootstrapper's loop. No subscribers for OnDisconnectedEvent or OnDisconnectedWithCause, and no callers for SetNickname or CurrentNickname. ConfigurePhotonSettings duplicates the dead NetworkManager version. This is the only live place that sets AutomaticallySyncScene=true, so keep that line.
proposed_action: In OnDisconnected, while the connector is still in its connecting state, raise OnConnectionFailed for any cause other than DisconnectByClientLogic/ApplicationQuit. Delete OnDisconnectedEvent, OnDisconnectedWithCause, SetNickname and CurrentNickname. Keep a single timeout (the connector's) and drop the duplicate wait in AuthBootstrapper, or the other way round.
dependencies: The loading screen and HomeConnectionWatcher behaviour after a failed first connect must be re-tested (no network at launch, airplane mode). Once in Home, HomeConnectionWatcher already handles drops.
verdict_reason: The bug is real. OnDisconnected (PhotonAuthConnector.cs:210-242) clears IsConnecting first. It raises OnConnectionFailed only for CustomAuthenticationFailed, InvalidAuthentication and AuthenticationTicketExpired; any other cause raises OnDisconnectedEvent, which has no subscribers. Because IsConnecting is now false, the connector's Update timeout never fires either. AuthBootstrapper.AuthenticationFlow (564-582) then waits its full 30 s before HandleError and retry. This happens only when PlayFab login succeeded but Photon failed, since PlayFab fails first when there is no network at all. AppLoadingView.Entrance (UIV2/Scripts/Core/AppLoadingView.cs:104) has a third 30 s realtime limit, so the user sees "Connessione non riuscita" at about 30 s. HomeConnectionWatcher.OnDisconnected acts only after startScreen.HasEntered, so boot-time failures are handled only by AuthBootstrapper. Other checks hold: OnDisconnectedEvent, OnDisconnectedWithCause, SetNickname and CurrentNickname have zero references. PhotonAuthConnector.IsConnected and the static Instance are also unused externally; the connector is AddComponent'ed and is in no scene. NetworkManager appears only in TESTPHOTN.unity and NetworkTestUI. PhotonAuthConnector.cs:198 is the only code line setting AutomaticallySyncScene=true. What's wrong is the "or the other way round" timeout option, which is unsafe. AuthBootstrapper.ReconnectPhoton (lines 292-295, comment at 294 "il limite di 30 s del connettore") waits only on PhotonIdle and relies on the connector's Update timeout calling PhotonNetwork.Disconnect. Removing the connector's timeout would let a stalled connect hang the rebind/reconnect coroutine forever. Implementation detail: wasConnecting must be captured before line 212 resets IsConnecting.
corrected_action:
In PhotonAuthConnector.OnDisconnected, capture `bool wasConnecting = IsConnecting;` before resetting it. Raise OnConnectionFailed(errorMessage) when (wasConnecting || cause is one of the three auth causes) and cause is neither DisconnectByClientLogic nor ApplicationQuit. The connector's own timeout already raises the failure and then Disconnects with DisconnectByClientLogic, so this does not double-fire.

Delete OnDisconnectedEvent, OnDisconnectedWithCause (and the else-branch invoking them), SetNickname, CurrentNickname and the unused IsConnected property. Keep ConfigurePhotonSettings, including AutomaticallySyncScene=true.

Keep the connector's Update timeout: ReconnectPhoton depends on it. AuthBootstrapper's 30 s loop in AuthenticationFlow can either stay as a harmless safety net or be reduced to `while (!photonConnectDone) yield return null;`. Never remove the connector's timeout instead.

Re-test both boot cases: Photon unreachable with PlayFab reachable, and airplane mode toggled during the Photon connect. Expect fast retries (1/2/4 s), then AppLoadingView's Riprova/Annulla. Also re-test HomeConnectionWatcher after entering. PhotonAuthConnector.cs is ASCII with CRLF.

title: Prototype "PhotonApplicationNotFound" branch marks auth Ready without Photon
evidence: Lines 503-522 treat a Photon "application not found" failure as success and set Ready offline. A real AppId is configured (PhotonServerSettings AppIdRealtime, and the photonAppIdOverride in MainMenu), so this only hides misconfiguration. Since 2.32 the AppVersion is pinned to Application.version, and a wrong AppId should surface as an error, not as a silent offline login.
proposed_action: Remove the branch and let it fall into the normal connection-failed path (offline-capable Home with HomeConnectionWatcher retry).
dependencies: none
verdict_reason: The branch is real (AuthBootstrapper.cs:503-522). A real AppId is configured: PhotonServerSettings.asset AppIdRealtime is set, and MainMenu.unity:484000 photonAppIdOverride is non-empty. Online play and Photon webhooks are live, so the PlayFab Photon add-on is configured and the branch never fires in production. The branch's ShowError text never reaches the user anyway: `_authUI` is always null. In MainMenu, authUIComponent (line 484004) points at fileID 1564524997, which is a CanvasScaler (m_UiScaleMode) and not an IAuthUI. RegisterAuthUI has no callers. The only IAuthUI implementer, LoginGateUI, is in no scene and is already on the FASE10 Block 3 deletion list. What's wrong is the claimed fallback, "offline-capable Home with HomeConnectionWatcher retry". The real path is HandleError: retry 3 times, then AuthState.Error, then AppLoadingView.Entrance shows Fail("Connessione non riuscita. Puoi riprovare.") with Riprova/Annulla on the login screen. StartScreenV2.Enter requires IsReady before CompleteEntrance, and HomeConnectionWatcher only acts after HasEntered. So if the add-on were ever misconfigured, nobody could enter the app at all, including offline training. That is consistent with every other token failure and is arguably correct, but the finding's description of the outcome is false.
corrected_action:
Delete AuthBootstrapper.cs lines 503-522, the whole `if (... "PhotonApplicationNotFound" ...)` block, so the failure goes to `yield return HandleError("Failed to get Photon token", photonTokenError)`. Correct the stated outcome: a misconfigured PlayFab Photon add-on now blocks entry. The loading screen shows "Connessione non riuscita" with Riprova/Annulla on the login screen; there is no offline Home. Behaviour in production is unchanged because the add-on is configured. Risk stays low. AuthBootstrapper.cs is UTF-8 with CRLF.

Optional follow-up, tied to FASE10 Block 3 (LoginGateUI deletion): IAuthUI, the authUIComponent field (it holds a CanvasScaler in MainMenu), _authUI, RegisterAuthUI, HandleDisplayNameChanged and every `_authUI?.` call in AuthBootstrapper become dead and can go in the same pass.

title: Client sends a forfeit opponent id ("avversario") the server ignores, and keeps a client-side forfeit cap mirror plus an opponent-id cache to feed it
evidence: RewardsService.cs:122 sets args["avversario"]=forfeitOpponent. 51.js never reads args.avversario: since 2.61 the opponent comes from the Shared Group match record (lines 396-397 and 550 mention it only in comments). test.js still passes avversario at lines 183, 194, 200 and 404. proposed_action: Stop sending avversario. Remove forfeitOpponent's id payload but keep a bool for 'won by forfeit', plus forfeitActor and the room name, which the server needs. Remove RememberOpponentIds, KnownOpponentId and KnownIdsKey from MatchResultsV2. Either drop the client ForfeitRewarded estimate (show the reward only after ServerXp arrives) or keep it consciously as UI optimism. Update test.js calls and ModerationViewTests to match. The server is untouched.
dependencies: Touches the forfeit reward contract, which is security-adjacent: verify against 51.js premioPartita and run `node Server/CloudScript/test.js` plus the EditMode tests. No CloudScript redeploy needed, since the server already ignores the arg. Check how the results screen behaves while waiting for the server reply.
verdict_reason: The core claim holds. In Server/CloudScript/51.js, premioPartita (lines 403-454) reads only args.abbandono, args.stanza and args.attore. avversario appears only in comments (51.js and 51.carica.js lines 396-397 and 550). It is passed in test.js at lines 183, 194, 200 and 404 but never asserted on. Problems with the finding: (1) Two paths are wrong. MatchResultsV2 is at Assets/UIV2/Scripts/Core/MatchResultsV2.cs, not Assets/Scripts/UIV2/. The test is at Assets/Tests/Editor/ModerationViewTests.cs:53-65, not Assets/Tests/EditMode. (2) The action contradicts itself. It removes RememberOpponentIds, KnownOpponentId and the id payload, yet offers to keep the ForfeitRewarded estimate, and that estimate needs the opponent id for its once-per-opponent dedupe. On the rejoin path (CheckOpponentsAfterRejoin, line 207), KnownOpponentId is the only source of that id. (3) A dependency is missing. The estimated xp is also written to local progress through PlayerProgressLocal.RecordGameResult(won, xp) at MatchResultsV2.cs:376. ServerXp (lines 394-402) corrects only the display, not local progress. Dropping the cap would let local XP over-count forfeits beyond the cap whenever the cloud profile is not loaded. (4) The comment at MatchResultsV2.cs:188-191 records an explicit user choice (02/10) to remember opponent ids across a restart. Removing it reverses a user decision. The PlayerPrefs keys "Partita.Avversari" and "Moderazione.AbbandoniPremiati" appear only in MatchResultsV2, so nothing else depends on them.
corrected_action: Step A, safe, no user decision. In Assets/Scripts/Auth/RewardsService.cs:122, stop setting args["avversario"] and keep args["abbandono"]=true. Fix the doc at lines 114-115. Optionally replace the string forfeitOpponent parameter with a bool forfeit. Drop the avversario: entries from Server/CloudScript/test.js lines 183, 194, 200 and 404, then run node Server/CloudScript/test.js. No CloudScript redeploy is needed. Step B, user decision because it reverses the 02/10 choice: drop the client forfeit-XP estimate entirely. In Assets/UIV2/Scripts/Core/MatchResultsV2.cs, delete MaxForfeitRewards (83), KnownIdsKey and nextIdsCheck (214-215), RememberOpponentIds (218-240) and its call at 608, KnownOpponentId (242-249), ForfeitRewarded (259-272) and the "Moderazione.AbbandoniPremiati" block (365-370). Turn forfeitOpponent into a bool, and keep forfeitActor and the room name. For forfeits, pass xp=0 to PlayerProgressLocal.RecordGameResult and the estimate, and let ServerXp show the real value, or explicitly accept local over-count. Delete ForfeitXp_ThreePerDay_OncePerOpponent_ResetsNextDay in Assets/Tests/Editor/ModerationViewTests.cs:53-65 and run the EditMode tests. If the user keeps the estimate, do only Step A: RememberOpponentIds and KnownOpponentId must then stay, and forfeitOpponent must stay a string.

title: The 60 s rejoin window and the 5-attempt limit are defined in several places
evidence: The 60 s window appears as MatchmakingManager.RejoinWindowMilliseconds=60000 (PlayerTtl), NetworkGameController.RejoinWindowSeconds=60f, ModerationService.SeatSeconds=60, and the dead NetworkConstants.RECONNECT_GRACE_PERIOD=60. The 5-attempt limit appears as NetworkGameController.MaxRejoinAttempts=5 and HomeConnectionWatcher.MaxAttempts=5. The reconnect loops in NetworkGameController.ReconnectAndRejoinLoop and HomeConnectionWatcher.Reconnect/Rejoin are near-identical (0.25 s poll, 3 s spacing, overlay updates). No mismatch today.
proposed_action: Make MatchmakingManager.RejoinWindowMilliseconds the single source. Derive NetworkGameController.RejoinWindowSeconds and ModerationService.SeatSeconds from it (all three are in Assembly-CSharp). Make HomeConnectionWatcher use NetworkGameController.MaxRejoinAttempts, or the reverse. Leave the two loops separate unless they get touched again; merging them is not worth the risk now.
dependencies: The NetworkConstants copy goes away with net-legacy-cluster. ModerationService is security-relevant: change only the constant's source, not the logic.
verdict_reason: Verified: MatchmakingManager.cs:74 RejoinWindowMilliseconds=60000 (used for PlayerTtl and EmptyRoomTtl at lines 106-107), NetworkGameController.cs:308 RejoinWindowSeconds=60f, ModerationService.cs:25 SeatSeconds=60 (lines 187 and 189), and NetworkTypes.cs:165 RECONNECT_GRACE_PERIOD=60f, which nothing reads. The only project asmdefs are Project51.Core and Project51.Gameplay, so Networking, Auth and UIV2 are all in Assembly-CSharp and cross-referencing these constants is legal. No external code reads these constants, including tests. The 60 s value must equal PlayerTtl, so a single source is justified. The attempt counts are a different matter. HomeConnectionWatcher.MaxAttempts governs both the Home Photon reconnect loop (Reconnect, lines 134-146, which is not a rejoin) and the restart rejoin (line 72). NetworkGameController.MaxRejoinAttempts governs the mid-match rejoin. These are separate UX policies that happen to share the value 5, not one duplicated fact, so coupling them adds a dependency without removing a real risk. NetworkConstants itself is still used by the legacy NetworkManager, RoomManager and NetworkTestUI, so only RECONNECT_GRACE_PERIOD is dead.
corrected_action: Limit the change to the 60 s window. In NetworkGameController.cs:308, write `public const float RejoinWindowSeconds = MatchmakingManager.RejoinWindowMilliseconds / 1000f;` (same namespace). In ModerationService.cs:25, write `public const int SeatSeconds = Project51.Networking.MatchmakingManager.RejoinWindowMilliseconds / 1000;`, changing only the constant's source and not the logic. Delete NetworkConstants.RECONNECT_GRACE_PERIOD (NetworkTypes.cs:165) now, or with the legacy cluster. Leave HomeConnectionWatcher.MaxAttempts and NetworkGameController.MaxRejoinAttempts independent. Comments that say '60 s' (ModerationService:22, HomeConnectionWatcher:52, MatchResultsV2:277) need no change.

title: Replace TurnController's three reflection calls into NetworkGameController with events (pattern already used)
evidence: TurnController (Project51.Gameplay asmdef) looks up NetworkGameController.Instance by reflection in three places: lines 671-686 (SendInitialGameState), 1416-1437 (SendInitialGameState/RequestResync) and 2044-2058 (SendAccuso). proposed_action: Add three static or instance events on TurnController (InitialStateReady, ResyncRequested, AccusoDeclared) and subscribe to them in NetworkGameController next to the existing ones. Delete the reflection blocks. Watch the ordering: NetworkGameController sets Instance in Awake but subscribes in Start, so make sure the initial-state send cannot fire before Start (subscribe in Awake/OnEnable, or use a static event).
dependencies: NetworkAccusoSyncTests must be updated. A multiplayer play test is needed: initial deal, resync after rejoin, accuso sync in 1v1/2v2. Optional: the user may prefer to leave working reflection alone.
verdict_reason: The reflection is real: TurnController.cs:676-686 calls SendInitialGameState, 1416-1437 calls SendInitialGameState on the master or RequestResync on a client, and 2047-2058 calls SendAccuso. All three use Type.GetType("Project51.Networking.NetworkGameController, Assembly-CSharp"). The comment at 672-675 records that an earlier assembly rename made this lookup fail silently, so the fragility is proven. The event pattern already exists: NGC.Start lines 212-214 subscribe OnLocalPlayerMoveRequested, OnMoveExecuted and SeatInactive, and OnDestroy 461-463 unsubscribes them. Wrong dependency: NetworkAccusoSyncTests (Assets/Tests/Editor, not EditMode) does not touch the reflection path. It tests only NetworkGameController.AlignAccusoTotal and RoundManager, so it needs no update. The ordering concern is lower than stated: in multiplayer, GameSceneInitializer.Start calls StartGame through Invoke(..., multiplayerStartDelay=0.5 s) (GameSceneInitializer.cs:78, GameScene.unity:149597), so NGC.Start has already subscribed. Resync and accuso happen mid-match, and clients also re-request the initial state themselves (NGC.cs:495). Incomplete scope: SetDealerIndicatorViaReflection (TurnController.cs:1109-1118, into PlayerBannerManager in Assembly-CSharp) uses the same pattern and should be converted or explicitly left. Doc comments that cite the reflection pattern must also change: TurnController.cs:1089, 1106-1107, 1388-1391, 2044-2046, and NGC.cs:505-510. A side note outside this area: GameSceneInitializer.cs:496 reflects into its own assembly (CameraResponsiveFit, Project51.Gameplay), which is pointless.
corrected_action: User decision first: the working reflection can be kept. If approved, add two instance events on TurnController. The first is `event Action<GameState> StateBroadcastRequested`, raised at both SendInitialGameState sites (676 and the master branch at 1431). The second is `event Action ResyncRequested`, raised at 1436. Add a third, `event Action<int,int> AccusoDeclared`, raised in TrySendAccusoSync. Subscribe and unsubscribe them in NGC.Start/OnDestroy next to the existing three; Start is enough because of the 0.5 s Invoke. Delete the three reflection blocks and update the comments listed above. Optionally also turn SetDealerIndicatorViaReflection into an event, or leave it and say so. NetworkAccusoSyncTests needs no change. Required check: run the EditMode tests, then a 2-device online test covering the initial deal reaching the client, a forced resync, accuso sync in 1v1 and 2v2, and a master switch. Update memory feedback_assembly_boundaries_gameplay_vs_ui (it cites TrySendAccusoSync as the reference pattern).

title: PlayerProgressLocal pendingExp machinery is legacy (nothing writes KEY_PENDING_EXP anymore)

verdict_reason: The core claim holds. (a) KEY_LEVEL is not read anywhere: it appears only in ResetAllProgress's DeleteKey, and Level is computed from Exp. (b) TotalWins and TotalGames are used internally by RecordGameResult, so they can only become private, not be deleted. Nothing outside the class reads them, so progress_wins and progress_totalGames are written but never displayed (dead data). If they are dropped, MatchResultsV2.cs:415 `RecordGameResult(false)` with 0 XP becomes a no-op. (c) OnLevelUp, ExpToNextLevel and LevelProgress have zero external hits: confirmed removable. TryAddExp can become private. (d) Live members to keep: Exp (HomeV2Integration:324, MatchResultsV2:374), Level (PlayerBannerManager:485), OnExpChanged (HomeV2Integration:124/405, UIV2FeedbackParticles:62-64/201, the latter live via RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod), RecordGameResult (MatchResultsV2:376/415), CreateInstance. Keep "progress_level" and "progress_pendingExp" in AccountPrefKeys. Rewrite the class summary.
